name: What is the difference between a room addition and an ADU?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a room addition and an ADU in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a room addition and an ADU in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A room addition increases the size of the main house and remains part of the primary residence. An ADU, by contrast, is a separate dwelling unit designed for independent living, usually with its own kitchen, bathroom, and sleeping area. That difference affects how the project is planned, permitted, and valued. For Los Angeles homeowners, the choice often depends on the goal. If the goal is a larger primary suite, family room, or expanded kitchen, a room addition is usually the better fit. If the goal is rental income, multigenerational living, or a private guest unit, an ADU may be more appropriate. The design and approval path can differ significantly between the two. Before choosing, homeowners should compare site constraints, utility connections, parking impacts, and resale implications. A project labeled as an addition may be easier to integrate aesthetically, while an ADU may offer stronger functional separation. The right answer depends on how the space will be used long term.
acceptedAnswer.description: A room addition expands the main home and becomes part of the existing house. An ADU is a separate independent living unit with its own kitchen and living function, and it often has different zoning, permit, and design requirements.
